children: AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo’s Enhertu reduced disease progression risk by 37% compared with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in a Phase III trial

AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo’s Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) as a first-line treatment for patients with unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic HER2-mutant non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

Results from the Phase III DESTINY-Lung04 trial, presented at the IASLC 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer in Seoul, showed median PFS of 14.3 months with Enhertu compared with 8.3 months for pembrolizumab plus platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy, the global standard of care.

The objective response rate was 70 per cent with Enhertu, compared with 44.5 per cent for pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy. Median duration of response was 13.4 months and 9.7 months, respectively. Julia Rotow, MD, Assistant Professor of Medicine at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and lead investigator of the trial, said, “With seventy per cent of patients responding and a median progression-free survival of 14.3 months, trastuzumab deruxtecan has the potential to become an important new first-line treatment option for these patients.”

Susan Galbraith, Executive Vice President, Oncology Haematology R&D, AstraZeneca, said the results add to evidence supporting Enhertu for patients with HER2 alterations and highlighted its potential use at metastatic diagnosis. John Tsai, Global Head, R&D, Daiichi Sankyo, said the six-month PFS benefit and response rates “reinforce the importance of targeting HER2 directly” and support the potential of Enhertu in the first-line setting.

Overall survival data were 46.9 per cent mature at the 9 June, 2026 data cut-off, and no formal hypothesis testing was conducted. Median OS was 29.3 months with Enhertu versus 33.1 months with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy. The companies noted that differences in subsequent therapies may affect interpretation of the interim OS results.

The safety profile was generally consistent with Enhertu’s established profile. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 34.1 per cent of patients receiving Enhertu and 33.6 per cent receiving pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy. Interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 20.8 per cent of Enhertu-treated patients, with most cases being Grade 1 or Grade 2. Four Grade 5 ILD events were reported.

Enhertu is already approved for previously treated metastatic NSCLC with activating HER2 mutations and certain HER2-positive solid tumours. It is a HER2-directed DXd antibody drug conjugate discovered by Daiichi Sankyo and jointly developed and commercialised by AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo.
